**Parent epic:** https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/19

**User Story:**
As a founder, I want to compare actual order contribution and working-capital needs, so I can reject unsustainable contracts.

**Epic:** E18 — B2B sales, customer success & commercialization  
**Domain:** Business development / Backend  
**Type:** Feature  
**Priority:** P1  
**Target Release:** C — Controlled pilot — after operational gates  
**Estimated Hours:** TBD — team estimate required  
**Story Points:** 5 — provisional source estimate  
**Sprint / Day:** Unscheduled  
**Assignee:** Unassigned  
**Owner Role:** Business development  
**Status:** Proposed  
**Source PDF Mapping:** Expanded product scope; no PDF story mapping  
**Suggested Labels:** `story`, `P1`, `release:C`, `epic:E18`, `business-development`, `backend`

**Dependencies:** [E10-01](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/142), [E10-05](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/66), [E10-08](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/63)
**Dependency Provenance:** Source blockers: —; additional proposed blockers: E10-01, E10-05, E10-08.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] Quote versus actual variance, buyer payment milestones, obligations and minimum cash gap calculated per order.
- [ ] Compare quoted versus actual revenue/cost lines with variance reasons.
- [ ] Model timing of buyer receipts, material purchases and artisan obligations.
- [ ] Show minimum cash gap and assumptions without conflating contribution with cash.
- [ ] Require finance review before committing to an unfunded or unsustainable new contract.

**Technical Notes / Deliverables:**

Use actual reconciled ledger data plus explicitly labeled forecasts; the report can inform subsequent pilots without depending on pilot completion.

**Verification / Evidence:**

Analyze profitable-but-cash-negative and loss-making examples; verify the dashboard exposes both risks separately.

**Completion Rule:** Attach evidence for all criteria and complete review. Verify applicable permissions, failure states and business invariants. Label synthetic results; individual wearable data never enters commerce.
title: [E18-03] Actual Contribution and Working-Capital Review

**User Story:**
As a finance manager, I want payment-timeliness metrics from contractual due dates and verified settlement events, so delay reporting is accurate.

**Epic:** E10 — Buyer finance, artisan payables, payouts & settlement  
**Domain:** Backend / Finance  
**Type:** Feature  
**Priority:** P1  
**Target Release:** C — Controlled pilot — after operational gates

**Assignee:** Unassigned

**Status:** Proposed

**Dependencies:** [E10-06](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/61), [E10-08](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/63)
**Dependency Provenance:** Source blockers: —; additional proposed blockers: E10-06, E10-08.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] On-time rate excludes missing/unknown denominators, distinguishes planned from completed, and identifies unverified payout dates.
- [ ] Derive due dates from accepted contractual rules rather than report creation dates.
- [ ] Compute on-time numerator/eligible denominator with explicit reporting period.
- [ ] Distinguish outstanding overdue, settled late, on-time and unknown/unverified dates.
- [ ] Define treatment of partial payments and disputed obligations and disclose exclusions.

**Technical Notes / Deliverables:**

Use versioned metric definitions and payout reconciliation timestamps; planned payment dates are not completed-payment evidence.

**Verification / Evidence:**

Evaluate on-time, late, unpaid and missing-date cases; verify rates and excluded counts against manual calculation.

**Completion Rule:** Attach evidence for all criteria and complete review. Verify applicable permissions, failure states and business invariants. Label synthetic results; individual wearable data never enters commerce.

**User Story:**
As a finance manager, I want a documented order financial-closure gate, so no unpaid artisan obligation is hidden when an order is closed.

**Epic:** E10 — Buyer finance, artisan payables, payouts & settlement  
**Domain:** Backend / Finance  
**Type:** Feature  
**Priority:** P1  
**Target Release:** C — Controlled pilot — after operational gates

**Dependencies:** [E09-05](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/60), [E10-08](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/63), [E10-05](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/66), [E10-10](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/72)
**Dependency Provenance:** Source blockers: E09-05, E10-08; additional proposed blockers: E10-05, E10-10.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- [ ] Closure blocks on unreconciled receivables, undisposed material costs, outstanding payables or open settlement disputes unless explicit authorized exception.
- [ ] Check buyer receivables, all artisan obligations, settlement disputes and material dispositions.
- [ ] Block closure when a required balance/evidence remains unresolved.
- [ ] Require a documented authorized and lawful disposition for any exception without erasing liability history.
- [ ] Record closure checklist, actor, time and ledger snapshot atomically.

**Technical Notes / Deliverables:**

Implement the CLOSED transition with finance/QA/logistics gates; a status toggle cannot bypass outstanding obligations.

**Verification / Evidence:**

Try closing with an unpaid artisan and open receipt discrepancy, then resolve them and verify one audited closure.

**Completion Rule:** Attach evidence for all criteria and complete review. Verify applicable permissions, failure states and business invariants. Label synthetic results; individual wearable data never enters commerce.
title: [E10-14] Guarded Financial Order Closure
